api.description: Caturus is an integrated U.S. natural-gas and LNG platform whose legal parent is Caturus Holdco, LLC, renamed from SoTex HoldCo in August 2025. The platform combines Caturus Energy's Texas upstream production with the controlled 9.5 mtpa Commonwealth LNG export project in Cameron Parish, Louisiana. After the May 14, 2026 CPP Investments closing, regulatory filings support a direct governance cap table of 52.6% Kimmeridge-managed interests, 24.1% Mubadala, 22.8% CPP Investments and 0.5% Caturus management. Caturus reported more than 1 Bcfe per day of net production across approximately 280,000 net acres after the Galvan Ranch acquisition, while Commonwealth LNG reached FID and closed project financing in May 2026. Caturus Energy and Commonwealth LNG are subordinate operating subsidiaries/projects, not separate manager-level PortCos, and project financiers are not parent owners. No later platform sale, owner exit, cancellation or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

Caturus is an integrated U.S. natural-gas and LNG platform whose legal parent is Caturus Holdco, LLC, renamed from SoTex HoldCo in August 2025. The platform combines Caturus Energy's Texas upstream production with the controlled 9.5 mtpa Commonwealth LNG export project in Cameron Parish, Louisiana. After the May 14, 2026 CPP Investments closing, regulatory filings support a direct governance cap table of 52.6% Kimmeridge-managed interests, 24.1% Mubadala, 22.8% CPP Investments and 0.5% Caturus management. CPP also has a disclosed economic look-through through Kimmeridge-managed funds, but that indirect interest carries no additional governance and public CPP percentages use a different aggregation basis; the 22.8% direct interest is therefore used for the ownership row. Kimmeridge's exact fund allocation and CPP's primary-versus-secondary mix are not publicly disclosed. Caturus reported more than 1 Bcfe per day of net production across approximately 280,000 net acres after the Galvan Ranch acquisition, while Commonwealth LNG reached FID and closed project financing in May 2026. Caturus Energy and Commonwealth LNG are subordinate operating subsidiaries/projects, not separate manager-level PortCos, and project financiers are not parent owners. No later platform sale, owner exit, cancellation or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

results.name: Pacifico Sur

api.name: Pacifico Sur
api.description: Pacifico Sur is the operating toll-road concession held through Concesionaria Autopista Guadalajara Tepic, S.A. de C.V. (CAGT). Its 309.6-kilometer network in Jalisco and Nayarit includes the Guadalajara–Tepic toll road, the South Guadalajara Bypass and the Tepic Bypass, serving freight, tourism and other toll-paying road users under a long-duration user-pay concession. A definitive agreement was announced on October 2, 2018 and the direct purchase of 49% of CAGT closed on May 15, 2019, leaving IDEAL with 51%, CPP Investments with 29% and Ontario Teachers' with 20%. A 2020 modification extended the concession to 60 years from November 30, 2011, implying expiry in November 2071. Pacifico Sur remains a separate direct PortCo from IDEAL Group and Autopista Arco Norte, and no later direct-stake sale, concession transfer or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

results.name: CARMA Corp.

api.name: CARMA Corp.
api.description: CARMA Corp. provides utility submetering, billing, collections, consumption reporting and on-site technical services for multi-residential, commercial and institutional properties. The company traces its predecessor operations to 1977 and was formed as CARMA Corp. through the August 2019 amalgamation of Carma Industries Inc. and Carma Billing Services Inc. CVC DIF agreed to acquire CARMA from TerraNova through DIF Infrastructure VIII on September 15, 2025, and industry-association reporting confirms the sale closed in December 2025. The disclosed acquisition vehicle is DIF Infra 8 Canada Holdco 2 Ltd.; the exact closing day, acquired stake and any management or family rollover are not publicly disclosed. CARMA operated more than 135,000 units across more than 1,000 buildings at signing and was reported to have approximately 350,000 meters installed across North America by June 2026. Spectrum, Priority Submetering, Undercurrent and Greensource remain operating businesses beneath CARMA rather than separate manager-level PortCos. No later sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.
